newsitem.title: SUDAN: Rival rebels in heavy fighting in south Sudan.
newsitem.headline: Rival rebels in heavy fighting in south Sudan.

text.p: Heavy fighting broke out between rival rebel groups in southern Sudan last week, a privately owned Sudanese newspaper reported on Thursday.

Alwan newspaper said the Bahr al-Ghazal group, led by Kerubino Kwanyin Bol, had seized Paning Bay area in Bahr al-Ghazal state and expelled the forces of John Garang's mainstream Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
The SPLA has been fighting the Khartoum government for 13 years for control of the south.
Bol broke away from the SPLA and signed a peace charter with the Islamist-backed government in April.
The paper quoted Faustino Atem, the military commander of Bol's group, as saying they had also seized large quantities of food from Garang's forces.
